title: National JOLTS mobility remains cool in January–July 2026, with July preliminary
source_unit: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey national total-nonfarm establishment rates from public series pages

denominator.unit: available monthly seasonally adjusted JOLTS rate observations

job_openings_rate_ytd.unit: percent arithmetic mean of January–July monthly rate

hires_rate_ytd.unit: percent arithmetic mean of January–July monthly rate

quits_rate_ytd.unit: percent arithmetic mean of January–July monthly rate

layoffs_and_discharges_rate_ytd.unit: percent arithmetic mean of January–July monthly rate

total_separations_rate_ytd.unit: percent arithmetic mean of January–July monthly rate

monthly_rates.unit: percent monthly seasonally adjusted rates, January through July

observations.method: Arithmetic mean of seven BLS seasonally adjusted monthly national JOLTS rates retrieved from the BLS public series pages; July is marked preliminary. Rates retain BLS establishment-based denominators and are not converted into individual transition probabilities.
observations.uncertainty: The partial-year values may be revised; July is preliminary; establishment rates summarize employer reports rather than unique workers, motivations, job quality, or household welfare. The public page vintage was extracted 2026-09-14.
observations.subgroup: Total nonfarm establishments; no worker demographic or occupation subgroup in this national series.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low quits can reflect reduced outside options, worker preference, retirement, sector composition, or measurement limits; stable openings can coexist with unequal mobility across occupations and groups.

observations.method: Transcribed the September 29, 2026 BLS JOLTS release tables and definitions. Levels are seasonally adjusted thousands; rates use BLS establishment-based denominators. The sector comparison is descriptive and is not a worker-level join to the Census nonemployer record.
observations.uncertainty: BLS reports establishments with payroll and excludes proprietors, partners, and unpaid family workers. The release says the August national measures were little changed; levels and rates do not identify unique workers, motivations, job quality, schedule control, pay, household welfare, or cultural meaning. Rounded release levels should not be reverse-engineered into exact counts.
observations.subgroup: Total nonfarm payroll establishments, with selected industry contrasts; no worker demographic or occupation subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: High openings and churn in health/social assistance and leisure/hospitality can reflect seasonal replacement, expansion, staffing difficulty, or sector composition rather than worker agency. Lower government churn does not establish better job quality or security.

boundary: This record extends the establishment-based JOLTS context through July 2026 using a partial-year public-page vintage. It does not establish worker bargaining power, individual job movement, job quality, pay, schedule control, household security, political meaning, or a causal effect of labor-market conditions. It must not be averaged with the complete 2026 annual mean because the year is incomplete and July is preliminary.
